tip: ना (na) tacked onto a command doesn't negate – it softens it into a plea: मत जाओ ना (mat jao na) = 'please don't go'.
Hindi often drops है (hai) after a negative: पसंद नहीं (pasand nahin) alone means 'doesn't like it' – no 'is' needed at the end.
जाना (jaana = go) glued onto a verb marks completion: रुक जाओ (ruk jao) = come to a full stop. Plain रुको (ruko) is just 'stop'.
'Not as...as' is a matched pair in Hindi: उतना साफ़ नहीं जितना (utna saaf nahin jitna) = literally 'not that-much clean, as-much-as'. Two words where English repeats 'as'.
Hindi says 'anywhere + not' where English says 'nowhere': कहीं भी शांति नहीं मिलती (kahin bhi shanti nahin milti) = literally 'anywhere peace is not found'.
न...न (na...na) means 'neither...nor' – a third negator besides नहीं (nahin) and मत (mat): न प्रिया आई, न कोई संदेश (na Priya aayi, na koi sandesh).
Skills 'come' to you in Hindi: तैरना आता ही नहीं (tairna aata hi nahin) = literally 'swimming just doesn't come (to me)' = I can't swim. आना (aana = to come) covers know-how.
Cars 'stand' in Hindi: खड़ी की (khari ki) = parked, literally 'made it stand'. गाड़ी खड़ी करना (gaadi khari karna) = to park a car.
'Not yet' = अभी तक...नहीं (abhi tak...nahin), literally 'until now not': मैंने अभी तक वह फ़िल्म नहीं देखी (maine abhi tak vah film nahin dekhi) = I haven't seen that film yet.
You 'drink' a cigarette in Hindi: सिगरेट मत पियो (cigarette mat piyo) = don't smoke, literally 'don't drink a cigarette'. पीना (peena) covers smoking too.
A command built on the infinitive is for later or gentler: देर मत करना (der mat karna) = 'don't be late (when the time comes)'. मत करो (mat karo) orders it right now.
